note: The code values the study prints with 'verify', and the rules it does not code at all. This is the owner's checklist. Nothing reads this file at run time; the values live in assets/js/build-here-rules.js (and, where 'code' says so, in another file). To clear an item: read the text named in 'clear', correct the value in the code if it differs, give it a checked date there (or drop verifyTag), then delete the item here. Until then the study shows the item in orange with 'verify' and never as a confirmed fact.

status.verify: A value is coded and printed, with 'verify' beside it, because the code text itself was not read.
status.not-coded: No value is coded. The study says so and tells the reader whom to ask. It never prints a 0 or a guess.
status.assumption: Not a code value. A drawing or planning assumption the study labels as one.

items.shows: House size (FinSize), year built, bedrooms and stories from the house-size files. FinSize is printed as the county's figure and is not used in the floor-area math. Stories prints with a note that the files may drop a half story.
items.from: scripts/build_index.py, which was not changed: it writes whole numbers, so 1.5 stories is stored as 1, and it keeps the first dwelling row of a parcel, so a second dwelling on the lot is not added. It does not check whether a row is active.
items.clear: Decide whether to change scripts/build_index.py (keep half stories, take the largest active dwelling row). Another page of the source site reads the same files, so check that page before changing the format.
